name: aidlc-native
description: AI-Native SDLC pipeline runner for VS Code, a fork of AIDLC. Drive Claude through the six-stage AI-Native SDLC Playbook — Plan → Design → Build → Test → Deploy → Maintain, where Maintain's incident loop opens the next Plan — step by step or unattended. Each epic owns its pipeline, depth and review gates: human-in-the-loop and headless auto-review gates, artifact annotation, requirements traceability, and an AIDLC Monitor with token usage & live observability. Also ships the classic AIDLC workflow and Spec Kit.

aidlcNative.autopilot.enabled.markdownDescription: 🚧 **Coming soon (experimental).** When enabled, starting an epic runs aidlc-autopilot: it collects epic context and generates a recommended plan (`context.json` + `autopilot-plan.md`) before the pipeline runs. Off by default while the feature is being tested.

aidlcNative.tokenMonitor.enabled.description: Show a status bar item with today/this-month Claude token spend, parsed from ~/.claude/projects logs.

aidlcNative.tokenMonitor.refreshSeconds.description: How often to re-scan ~/.claude/projects for new usage records (seconds, minimum 15).

aidlcNative.tokenMonitor.suggestionWindo.description: Window the cost-suggestion engine scans (in days). Older logs are skipped — they don't reflect current habits.

aidlcNative.monitor.enabled.description: Show a status bar item that polls the agents-observe server and opens the unified Monitor panel (Token Usage + Agents). Has no effect when agents-observe isn't running.

aidlcNative.monitor.pollIntervalSeconds.description: How often to poll the agents-observe server (GET /api/status) for the status bar and Monitor panel (seconds). Polling pauses while the window is unfocused.

aidlcNative.astGraph.enabled.description: Build a code graph of the workspace in the background and register it as a Claude MCP server so Claude can read structural code context cheaply. The engine is chosen by `aidlcNative.astGraph.engine`.

enumDescriptions: ast-graph (default): scans into .ast-graph/graph.db. Rescans on branch switch / pull; each scan rewrites the whole graph, which is slow on very large repos.

CodeGraph (opt-in, github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph): indexes into .codegraph/ once; its MCP server then watches the project and syncs only changed files. Better for large repos. Maps AIDLC's ast-graph tool names onto codegraph_explore via the CLAUDE.md hint.
aidlcNative.astGraph.engine.markdownDescription: Which code-graph engine backs the MCP server. Switching needs a window reload; the extension removes the other engine's MCP registration and CLAUDE.md block.

aidlcNative.astGraph.rescanOnSave.description: ast-graph only: rescan after source files change. Off by default — every ast-graph scan rewrites the whole graph, so on a large repo it keeps a core busy after each save. Branch switch / merge / pull always trigger a rescan. (CodeGraph syncs on save by itself.)

aidlcNative.astGraph.autoRescanDebounceS.description: Debounce window for rescans after git ref changes, and after source file saves when `aidlcNative.astGraph.rescanOnSave` is on (seconds).

aidlcNative.astGraph.codegraphTelemetry.description: CodeGraph only: allow CodeGraph's anonymous usage telemetry for the processes this extension starts. Off by default (sets CODEGRAPH_TELEMETRY=0).

aidlcNative.mcp.listTimeoutSeconds.description: Timeout (seconds) for `claude mcp list` in the MCP Servers panel. Claude health-checks every configured server, so raise this if you have many remote/unauthenticated servers and see a timeout.

aidlcNative.workspace.epicsDirectory.description: Relative path (from the project root) where epics are stored. Changing this updates `state.root` in workspace.yaml. The epic list and Start Epic wizard use this directory immediately.

aidlcNative.claude.configDir.markdownDescription: Claude Code config directory this window uses — the account behind `~/.claude`. Leave empty to use `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if set, else `~/.claude`. Set it (e.g. `~/.claude-work`) when you keep several Claude accounts and want this workspace pinned to one: workflow agents/skills, the annotation tools, the epic-memory hook, MCP registration, the token monitor and every `claude` terminal AIDLC opens all follow it. Reload the window after changing. Easier than editing this by hand: run **AIDLC: Switch Claude Account** (also on the status bar), which picks from `#aidlcNative.claude.configDirs#`.

aidlcNative.claude.configDirs.markdownDescription: Saved Claude accounts offered by **AIDLC: Switch Claude Account**. This list only names the accounts — the one actually in use is `#aidlcNative.claude.configDir#`, which is per-workspace, so several windows can hold different accounts at the same time. Example: `[{ "label": "Work", "path": "~/.claude-work" }]`.

label.description: Name shown in the picker and the status bar. Defaults to the folder name.

aidlcNative.claude.planUsage.enabled.markdownDescription: Show how much of the Claude plan the active account has used (5-hour and weekly windows) on the status bar, in the account tooltip, and in **AIDLC: Switch Claude Account**. Read from the signed-in account with the same call Claude Code's own `/usage` makes — that endpoint is not documented, so the indicator hides itself rather than guessing when it stops answering. Turn off to make no network call at all. Distinct from `#aidlcNative.tokenMonitor.enabled#`, which reports spend from local logs, not remaining quota.

enumDescriptions: One percentage per limit window — `5h 49% - 2h12m · 1w 66%`, and `5h 20% · 1w 40% · fable 88%` on a plan that reports a weekly window per model. Up to four windows, session first.
A single percentage: whichever window is closest to its limit.
aidlcNative.claude.planUsage.statusBar.markdownDescription: How much the plan-usage status bar item says. Percentages are what is **used**, as `/usage` reports them and matching the tooltip. The colour thresholds below are still set in percent **left**. Requires `#aidlcNative.claude.planUsage.enabled#`.

aidlcNative.claude.planUsage.showResetIn.markdownDescription: Show when the 5-hour window rolls over next to its percentage on the status bar — `5h 49% - 2h12m`. Only that window: a weekly one resets days out, which is a fact nobody plans the next hour around. The tooltip always lists every window's reset time.

aidlcNative.claude.planUsage.warnBelowPe.markdownDescription: Turn the status bar amber when the window that gates every model — the 5-hour or all-models weekly one — drops below this much **left**. A weekly window for a single model can also raise amber, but never red: the fix there is to run the next step on another model.

aidlcNative.claude.planUsage.criticalBel.markdownDescription: Turn the status bar red when a gating window drops below this much **left**. Clamped to at most `#aidlcNative.claude.planUsage.warnBelowPercent#`, since a critical threshold above the warning one would mean red never fires. The server's own severity — overage, a locked window — still goes red whatever this says.

aidlcNative.claude.planUsage.refreshSeco.markdownDescription: How often to re-read the remaining plan usage, in seconds. Minimum 60 — the windows move slowly and this is a shared endpoint.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with AIDLC
walkthroughs.description: Drive Claude through any pipeline declared in workspace.yaml — visually, from the editor.

steps.title: Welcome to AIDLC
steps.description:
AIDLC turns a single `workspace.yaml` into a runnable pipeline of Claude agents — edit it visually, run epics step-by-step, approve or reject each handoff.

The fastest way to feel it is to load the demo project in the next step.

steps.title: Load the demo project
steps.description:
One click scaffolds a full pipeline plus 6 sample epics into your current folder — no YAML to write.
[Load Demo Project](command:aidlcNative.loadDemoProject)

steps.title: Open the Workspace Builder
steps.description:
Visual editor for your agents, skills, and pipelines. Add an agent, swap its model, edit a skill inline.
[Open Workspace Builder](command:aidlcNative.openBuilder)

steps.title: Run your first epic
steps.description:
Pick a sample epic and watch Claude work through the pipeline. Approve, reject, or rerun any step.
[Open Epics List](command:aidlcNative.openEpicsList) · [Start Epic](command:aidlcNative.startEpic)

steps.title: Drive runs from the terminal
steps.description:
One-click zsh terminal in the bottom panel with the Claude CLI auto-launched. Use slash commands or run `aidlc` directly.
[Open Claude CLI Terminal](command:aidlcNative.openClaudeTerminal)

steps.title: Build your own workspace
steps.description:
Scaffold a fresh `.aidlc/workspace.yaml`, add custom skills/agents/pipelines, save the result as a reusable template.
[Init Sample Workspace](command:aidlcNative.initWorkspace) · [Add Skill](command:aidlcNative.addSkill) · [Add Agent](command:aidlcNative.addAgent) · [Save as Template](command:aidlcNative.savePreset)

scripts.copy:annotron: rm -rf vendor && node -e "require('fs').mkdirSync('vendor', { recursive: true })" && cp -R ../../vendor/annotron vendor/annotron
scripts.compile: pnpm copy:templates && pnpm copy:tools && pnpm copy:annotron && tsc -p ./ && vite build
scripts.watch: trap 'kill 0' SIGINT EXIT; pnpm watch:tsc & pnpm watch:webviews & wait
scripts.package: pnpm copy:templates && pnpm copy:tools && pnpm copy:annotron && pnpm typecheck && pnpm clean:out && pnpm bundle:webviews && pnpm bundle:prod && vsce package --no-dependencies
